name: Hindutva
summary: Hindutva is the Hindu nationalist ideology formulated by V. D. Savarkar in 1923, which defines the Indian nation by shared land, descent and Hindu culture rather than by religious creed. Its adherents, the Sangh Parivar (RSS, VHP and BJP), seek a culturally Hindu state, territorial unity (Akhand Bharat), a common civil law, protection of the cow and regulation of religious conversion. Scholars debate whether its treatment of Muslims and Christians as outsiders to the Hindu holy land is exclusionary, and its economics have shifted between swadeshi and market liberalism.
scope: The mainstream political Hindutva of Savarkar's Hindutva (1923), Golwalkar's We, or Our Nationhood Defined (1939) and the RSS-BJP movement as it exists today, with the BJP as its governing arm. Answers follow the present-day majority view, with notes where early texts like Golwalkar's are harsher than current public statements. It excludes Hinduism as a religion and Hindu reform movements apart from Hindutva.

keyFigures.name: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar
keyFigures.role: Author of Essentials of Hindutva (1923), which gave the term its political meaning.

keyFigures.name: M. S. Golwalkar
keyFigures.role: Long-time head of the RSS and early proponent of the Hindu Rashtra.

keyFigures.name: K. B. Hedgewar
keyFigures.role: Founder of the RSS, inspired by Savarkar's Hindutva.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not doctrinal; the BJP expands state-backed health cover (Ayushman Bharat) within a welfare-for-the-poor pitch.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No doctrinal position; the movement's economics are framed around growth and the poor, not wage floors.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Split between the swadeshi, integral-humanist wing and the neoliberal growth emphasis of the BJP's 1998-2004 government.

public-ownership.rationale: Integral humanism favours decentralised, human-centred economics, and the BJP in office has leaned towards privatisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The BJP governments pursued pro-growth, business-friendly policy; no doctrinal call for heavier wealth taxes.

unions-good.rationale: The Sangh has its own labour wing but stresses harmony over class struggle, so adherents are mixed.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is not central to Hindutva texts; practice mixes private enterprise with state projects.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No doctrinal stance; swadeshi voices favour curbing foreign firms while the government courts investment.

cut-welfare.rationale: The BJP's own manifesto pillars include the poor and farmers, so welfare is kept and branded.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker ownership is a socialist idea; Hindutva prefers class harmony within existing property forms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: A security-first nationalist outlook with an aggressive stance on terror favours state monitoring.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents back laws protecting Hindu sentiment but resist hate-speech laws they see as aimed at them.

strong-leader.rationale: Jaffrelot notes Hindutva differs from fascism in not centring on a single leader, though adherents admire decisive leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: The nation and its territorial unity are central to Hindutva; the state is a vehicle of the Hindu nation, not an evil.

limit-guns.rationale: No stated position; adherents are not organised around gun policy.

empower-police-military.rationale: The BJP's 1998-2004 government took a more aggressive defence and anti-terror stance.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

decide-locally.rationale: Stress on Akhand Bharat and the unity and integrity of the country, and revocation of Kashmir's autonomy in 2019, favour central authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

traditional-family.rationale: Social conservatism is a listed part of BJP ideology and the movement upholds Hindu family and cultural norms.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The BJP is socially conservative; the movement has been wary of legalising it, though views among adherents vary.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

more-religion-public.rationale: Modi's statement that Ram is the faith and policy of India and the Ayodhya temple show public Hindu symbolism, though the Sangh calls it cultural.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The movement's organ opposed expanded caste reservations (Mandal), and adherents prefer social harmony to group-targeted remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural nationalism is Hindutva's core: Hindu culture (sanskriti) is one of Savarkar's three essentials.

gradual-change.rationale: Described as cultural and revolutionary conservatism; adherents emphasise continuity of civilisation more than rupture.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Concern over undocumented Bangladeshi immigration, together with citizenship preference for non-Muslim migrants, implies restriction.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalist-centred foreign policy makes pooling sovereignty in global bodies unattractive.

free-trade.rationale: Split between swadeshi protectionists and the growth-and-globalisation line of the 1998-2004 government.

nation-first.rationale: The BJP's foreign policy is described as based on nationalist principles, and the Hindu nation comes first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Nationalist foreign policy emphasises sovereignty and national interest.

open-borders.rationale: Territorial integrity, citizenship tied to nation and CAA religious criterion all cut against open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: The BJP prioritises growth and manufacturing; no doctrinal limit on growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The BJP stresses development and technology as national goals.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Aggressive defence stance and development emphasis suggest support for nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Hindutva seeks electoral and cultural change; revolution is not its method.

experts-over-public.rationale: A populist-majoritarian style distrusts elites; scholars note friction with academics.

central-planning.rationale: Integral humanism describes an indigenous, human-centred alternative, not Soviet planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

basic-income.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Swadeshi strand favours protecting domestic industry; manufacturing-hub goals fit.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The BJP's current programme directs state support towards strategic sectors such as manufacturing.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Integral humanism favours a decentralised, human-centred economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Integral humanism has an organic-society flavour, but the movement has no state-bodies programme.

one-party-rule.rationale: Hindutva organisations compete in elections, and Jaffrelot says the movement treats the state as secondary to society.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The BJP operates within a republic; monarchy is not on its agenda.

democracy-best.rationale: The BJP presents itself as a democratic party, though scholars note tension with majoritarianism.

direct-votes.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

workers-councils.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

right-to-secede.rationale: The unity and integrity of the country is non-negotiable, and Bhagwat says there will be no compromise on it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Savarkar opposed caste hierarchy; modern leaders speak of social harmony, though critics see Brahminism.

political-violence-never.rationale: Violence linked to the movement is documented, and Savarkar's tradition did not renounce it.

war-builds-character.rationale: Golwalkar praised martial race pride, but mainstream adherents are not organised around this claim.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Hindutva judgments equate Hindutva with a way of life, and the movement attacks Western-style secularism as favouring minorities.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Savarkar said Hindutva is not primarily about theocratic dogma; the claim is cultural, not scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

military-superiority.rationale: The BJP's defence posture is described as aggressive and nationalist.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Savarkar's three essentials include common race and culture, and scholars describe cultural nationalism shading into ethnic nationalism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Hindutva makes the Hindu nation, not class, the primary unit.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Hindutva claims Hindus as the indigenous nation of India, so special land authority for other groups is not endorsed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

civilizational-union.rationale: Golwalkar's cultural map of the Hindu civilisation took in Afghanistan, Burma and Sri Lanka, and Akhand Bharat is a shared ideal.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Integral humanism rejects individualist self-interest as the basis of society.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Golwalkar's organic nation puts the national community first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

limit-population.rationale: Sangh leaders have voiced concern about demographic change, inclining towards population measures.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

restore-past-order.rationale: Hindutva looks to a golden age and civilisational revival, described as revolutionary conservatism.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Hindutva is an ideology of identity and not a pragmatic technocracy.

organic-representation.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

universal-morality.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Hindu nation as a self-governing people is central to the doctrine.

force-without-un.rationale: A nationalist foreign policy prioritises national interest over multilateral approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Adherents treat myth as history and religion as a basis of identity.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Golwalkar would limit rights of non-Hindus; benefits for citizens over foreigners follow.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

class-collaboration.rationale: Deoras and Bhagwat promoted social harmony and unity over class and caste conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving and reviving Hindu heritage is central.

dominated-front.rationale: India's nationalism looks to its own strength more than to a common front.

workers-nation.rationale: Nation, not class, is the organising unit.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Social conservatism, but no stated legal programme.

ban-interest.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Savarkar and the Sangh claim to include all Hindus; formal segregation by race law is not a programme.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Golwalkar says non-Hindus must adopt Hindu culture and language and revere Hindu religion, or stay wholly subordinate.

elite-replacement.rationale: Demographic anxiety exists but not a doctrine that elites plan replacement.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

national-mission.rationale: A vishwaguru idea exists, but it is not a regime export mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The BJP campaigns on anti-corruption and against dynastic elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The movement defends security forces, as in Kashmir.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Hindutva wants a state that serves cultural national purposes.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Opposition is framed around religion (love jihad) and not race.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Golwalkar denies minorities equal rights, while the modern movement claims equal rights for all citizens; adherents are split.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not a stated Hindutva position; inferred from its cultural-nationalist outlook and the BJP's record.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Hindutva reads Hindus as indigenous and sympathises with Israel as a restored homeland.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Hindutva leaders call for one civil law for all and the BJP pledged it in 2024.

restrict-conversion.rationale: BJP-ruled states have passed conversion laws with prison terms.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cow reverence is central and BJP-ruled states have passed slaughter bans.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Hindutva treats Hindu culture as the national culture and the Sangh runs Hindu-values schools; inferred from the "way of life" framing and its rejection of Western-style secularism (s1).

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The statement is about a socialist state, which Hindutva does not hold; its own state-strengthening stance is cultural-national, so the question does not apply cleanly.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The BJP claims democratic legitimacy through elections, but Hindutva grounds the nation in land, descent and culture rather than contract; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Adherents attack colonial and Marxist historiography as biased, yet claim their own account is true; split; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: The BJP's swadeshi and self-reliance lines favor domestic production and exports, though liberalization has also opened markets; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Golwalkar wanted non-Hindus subordinate rather than removed, and the present line claims equal citizenship; some militants differ; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Savarkar's Hindutva stresses military strength and national defense, so force is justified beyond defense; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Integral humanism favors organic harmony over struggle, while Golwalkar admires national vigor; adherents are split; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: BJP governments have banned organizations deemed extremist, and the movement favors a strong state against threats to national unity; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Hindutva texts stress duty and the nation over individual liberty and say little on non-domination; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The BJP is formally constitutional but favors a strong centre, and the doctrine has no firm line on separated powers; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Hindutva rejects class politics and has no vanguard doctrine, though the RSS is a disciplined cadre body; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Integral humanism's Antyodaya principle puts the last person first and the BJP pitches welfare for the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not doctrinal; BJP governments promote home ownership and the movement leans to property ownership; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from the BJP's pro-growth stance and its labour-code reforms tightening strike rules.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Population control and demographic concerns recur in Sangh Parivar rhetoric; inferred, not a founding doctrine.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Hindutva grounds the nation in shared land, descent and culture (Savarkar), though public statements stress unity in diversity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical, cultural-nationalist view of leadership; no source backs sortition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The RSS was banned in the 1975 Emergency and the BJP condemns it, but it favours a strong security state; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: BJP governments use stock limits and price measures on essential goods; inferred, not doctrinal.

party-controls-media.rationale: No doctrinal call for state media control; the BJP formally supports a free press; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Hindutva accepts civilian, constitutional command of the army and has no party-army doctrine; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from its civilisational view of nationhood and the Citizenship Amendment Act's religion-based path to citizenship.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not a doctrinal issue; inferred from the BJP's ordinary salaried governing practice and its caste-and-culture rather than pay-equality focus.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from the RSS-BJP's cadre-organisation model, where the party line binds members once set.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva's nationalism and territorial Akhand Bharat aims, which favour national sovereignty over shared supranational bodies.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The BJP governs within India's parliamentary system and Hindutva texts take no stand on presidential control; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Hinduism has no bishops and Hindutva defines the nation by culture, not church; no answer follows from its principles.

clerical-rule.rationale: Hindutva is a cultural-national ideology that Savarkar distinguished from Hinduism as religion, so it seeks a Hindu-cultural state rather than rule by religious scholars.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Hindutva is built on the primacy of the nation and its adherents back national defence, so working for one's own government's defeat is alien to it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from Sangh Parivar groups' campaigns against works they call offensive to Hindu culture and morals.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Hindutva has no position on term limits; inferred from the BJP's acceptance of a prime minister serving without limit.

recall-officials.rationale: Hindutva never addressed recall and India has no national recall mechanism; adherents have no common line.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: India's strategic autonomy tradition avoids formal alliances, but the BJP strengthens partnerships and a strong military; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: BJP economic policy accepts private property and markets; abolishing renting is not on its agenda.

people-in-arms.rationale: Savarkar urged militarising Hindu society, but the movement backs a strong professional army alongside the RSS's paramilitary-style training; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Integral humanism and swadeshi stress village-based India and traditional values over urban modernity; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Akhand Bharat, the undivided Indian homeland, is a stated Sangh Parivar aim, and Savarkar defined the nation by one fatherland.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Sangh Parivar rhetoric attacks westernised and left-liberal elites as detached from Indian people; inferred from its populist pitch.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Golwalkar and Savarkar present Hindu culture as the national culture to which others must conform, ranking it above others.

death-penalty.rationale: The BJP backs the death penalty for terrorism and heinous crimes; inferred from its law-and-order stance.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Social conservatism leads the movement to resist sex education and gender-equality curricula as foreign to Indian values; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Hindutva figures promote Vedic accounts of origins and have contested evolution, but it is not a doctrinal program and adherents differ.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Social conservatism favours obscenity laws; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Savarkar's test of shared fatherland, descent and holy land, and the CAA's religious criterion, tie citizenship to lineage and culture.

minority-language-support.rationale: The movement promotes Hindi and Sanskrit as national languages and resists regional or minority language claims.

religious-exemptions.rationale: It backs a uniform civil code and opposes separate personal laws or exemptions for minorities.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Emphasis on conformity to national Hindu culture and traditional social order leaves little room for encouraging eccentricity; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Nothing in Hindutva texts addresses debt relief; inferred from the BJP government's orthodox fiscal and creditor-friendly practice.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva stresses cultural and civilizational nationhood over economic transformation, and the BJP has favoured market reform.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred: the BJP governs under and defends the 1950 constitution, though it seeks changes such as a common civil code within it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: No stated position; adherents split between a strong-state, development-first tradition and the movement's formal commitment to democracy.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva's priority on duties to the Hindu nation; India itself has been a net recipient and is not framed around a duty of the rich.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from the BJP's nuclear-weapons stance (the 1998 tests) and its emphasis on national strength; not a doctrinal text position.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: No stated position; the BJP works within a parliamentary system, and adherents are not agreed on a presidential model.

central-bank-independence.rationale: No stated position; swadeshi and market-liberal strands of the movement differ on monetary policy.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Hindutva claims the whole of Akhand Bharat as the Hindu holy land and fatherland, which makes ceding claimed homeland for peace contrary to its core idea.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from the dharmic idea of duty and the swadeshi/trusteeship strand; property rights are not a defining issue.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The movement has no position on the nature of the USSR; its hostility to communism does not turn on this classification.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common line on environmental precaution, so this is left neutral.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from the BJP's security-minded, pro-military stance; Hindutva has no doctrine on alliance commitments.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from the Akhand Bharat claim and the Kashmir position, which treat Pakistan-held Kashmir as Indian land under illegitimate control.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: the RSS-BJP movement is itself party-political and Hindu-cultural, but it does not claim the figurehead presidency should be partisan.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from Akhand Bharat and the BJP's revocation of Article 370, which assert Indian territorial integrity over separatist claims.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The BJP revoked Article 370 and wants one common civil code and 'one nation', which cuts against special legal systems for regions.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Savarkar's Hindutva is a cultural-national doctrine, and modern Hindutva does not seek a divine-descent ruler; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: BJP economics shifted between swadeshi and liberalisation and the party has no flat-tax doctrine.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva stresses shared culture and descent as shaping the nation, with no settled view on nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from the dharmic tradition that rulers are bound by dharma and from the BJP's constitutional-democratic framing.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from the BJP government's national pride in the space programme (ISRO); not a Hindutva doctrine.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed by Hindutva thought; no common view among adherents.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from the strong personal leadership culture around the BJP's leader; contested among adherents and critics.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not a Hindutva issue; adherents have no common position on custody law.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred: integral humanism stresses social harmony over class conflict.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred: the BJP governments have not pursued land redistribution and stress property and growth.

refugee-return.rationale: Split: Hindutva champions return of Kashmiri Pandits but resists return or settlement of other refugee groups.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Akhand Bharat claims a cultural and territorial unity of the subcontinent as the Hindu holy land and fatherland.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: No doctrine of punishing apostasy; conversion is regulated through anti-conversion laws, which target inducement.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred: BJP-led governments have backed hijab restrictions, and Hindutva supports no legal covering for women.

common-currency.rationale: No doctrinal position on monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Akhand Bharat envisions the peoples of the Indian subcontinent as one cultural nation across current borders.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Golwalkar says non-Hindus must adopt Hindu culture or stay subordinate, and Hindutva backs a common civil code.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva sees India as the homeland of persecuted Hindus abroad, as with the Citizenship Amendment Act.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred: a cultural-nationalist movement opposed to Marxism, with culture and civilisation in the foreground.

no-bailouts.rationale: No doctrinal position; the BJP has both rescued banks and criticised bailouts.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva stresses the majority-community nation and the BJP has clashed with courts over appointments.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred: the BJP backed a one-third women's reservation, short of parity.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The swadeshi strand favours self-reliance, though the BJP has also liberalised trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: India has resisted linking labour and environmental conditions to trade deals.

moral-incentives.rationale: Integral humanism stresses duty, but there is no doctrine replacing material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred: the RSS organises through cultural and political work rather than armed vanguards.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva rejects caste hierarchy in Savarkar's formulation, and the Jana Sangh opposed princely privileges.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Hindutva defines the nation by Hindu civilization and the Sangh Parivar has pushed for school history centred on Indian and Hindu heritage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Hindutva is rooted in anti-colonial nationalism and rejects British rule, though some leaders spoke of Hindu culture's superiority; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: The RSS and BJP stress national pride and reverence for the nation, flag and Vande Mataram as core to education and character.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Race is not the Indian frame; the movement is split over caste reservations, so the statement does not map cleanly. Inferred from the caste debate in s1.

public-money-creation.rationale: The movement has no doctrine on money creation; swadeshi and market-liberal wings differ.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not doctrinal, but the BJP's growth-oriented record assumes capitalism can sustain itself; it rejects Marxist crisis theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Akhand Bharat, the idea of a cultural India stretching across the subcontinent, implies cultivating influence in lands once part of historic India.

delink-world-market.rationale: Swadeshi voices favour self-reliance, but the BJP in government courts global trade and investment.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The movement rejects Marxist class analysis and frames India as the exploited party, not workers in rich countries; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Hindutva does not stress libertarian property rights and its stated aims include social unity; inferred, though caste and community practices complicate this.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The movement works within India's Constitution and its Fundamental Rights, but it favours majoritarian cultural priorities; adherents are split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Hindutva's Akhand Bharat claim treats the partition of the Indian homeland as illegitimate, so a colonial-era division is inferred to lack force; no doctrine on treaties as such.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from the BJP's acceptance of parliamentary democracy and elections; the movement has no program on hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from majoritarian nationhood and the BJP's rejection of religion-based minority entitlements; not directly addressed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not addressed in Hindutva texts; adherents would split between order-first and rule-of-law views.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from the BJP's role as a governing party in a parliamentary republic; monarchy is not an issue for the movement.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Reverence for the cow and Hindu traditions of non-violence imply concern for animals, though it is not doctrinal beyond cattle.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from the cow-protection stance, which bars cattle slaughter but not other animal use; the movement does not address research.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from integral humanism's duty-centred, community-minded social ethic as described for the BJP; not a stated doctrine.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Hindutva calls on Hindus to organise and act politically, and the RSS builds a mass organisation; withdrawal contradicts that.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's own cultural-mobilisation strategy, which treats culture as a political resource rather than a pacifier.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Marxist concept foreign to Hindutva; its adherents would reject the framing, though they stress cultural hegemony of their own kind.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Swadeshi strands blame colonial extraction but the BJP embraces market liberalisation, so adherents are split.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the view that those born in the Hindu fatherland and holy land form the nation, and the CAA's citizenship tests; no explicit program.

party-own-road.rationale: Not applicable to the movement, which is anti-communist and has no party-to-party line.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Swadeshi and self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) are standard themes, though the BJP also courts foreign investment.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Akhand Bharat envisions reunifying the partitioned subcontinent, and the BJP backs claims over Pakistan-held Kashmir.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Hindutva holds Hindus to be the indigenous people of India and rejects any claim that they are settlers or that others have indigenous priority.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The RSS is opposed to the left and sees the Indian Constitution's secularism as appeasement; inferred, not a stated position.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The Sangh Parivar opposes communism strongly and early RSS texts admired European fascist nationalism; inferred that adherents condemn communism more than fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed in Hindutva sources; the question is American and has no bearing on the movement.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of Hindu monuments and heritage and its stress on civilisational continuity; not addressed directly.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; no doctrine, adherents split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed; no doctrine, adherents split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Hindutva holds Indian civilisation to be distinct, with its own cultural foundation, and rejects Western secularism as the model for India.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The RSS stresses discipline and civil society rather than military politics, and the BJP accepts civilian control of the armed forces.

paid-care-work.rationale: Hindutva sources favour traditional family roles and unpaid domestic work is not a movement demand.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from Hindu dharmic norms of respect for elders, which Hindutva writers draw on; not a political doctrine.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva as a governing movement works through elections and parliamentary politics.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the swadeshi strand of Hindutva economics noted by scholars, though liberalisation has weakened it.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on traditional family values and the sanctity of marriage.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: the movement works through disciplined organisation and standard parliamentary terms, not recall.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Adherents split: economics has shifted between swadeshi and market liberalism and is not doctrinal.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: the BJP defends private property, though the land is called the holy motherland.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the BJP as a governing party in a parliamentary democracy.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist aim of a common Hindu-culture public life, notably Hindi, and Golwalkar on cultural unity.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist view that the land is the Hindu holy land and belongs to its nation.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva opposes group-based preferences and holds that equal citizens are treated alike by law.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Adherents split between swadeshi and spiritual-simplicity themes and a pro-market government.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred: the movement accuses Pakistan of backing insurgents in India and stresses sovereignty.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on national sovereignty and territorial integrity.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred: the BJP is accused of cronyism yet is pro-business; Hindutva texts do not address lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: the Sangh Parivar distrusts foreign-funded missionary and NGO activity, and BJP governments have tightened foreign-contribution rules.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva rhetoric stresses Hindu demographic strength, and RSS leaders have urged larger families.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: not a doctrinal issue; BJP-run states have land-purchase limits but the movement has no common line.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: the BJP prefers market-friendly growth and targeted welfare over guaranteed employment.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva texts do not address democratic peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva stresses duty (dharma) to the nation and its order, which is at odds with a right to disobey.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred: sovereignty rhetoric favours non-intervention, but Hindutva also claims a stake in the protection of Hindus abroad.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: not addressed in the doctrine; the RSS-linked union is organised by industry but the movement has no stated view.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: Golwalkar treats Muslims and Christians as outsiders to the nation, and the movement's rhetoric on conversion and 'love jihad' implies this view.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva upholds the family and traditional marriage as national institutions.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: not a defining issue; the BJP has both defended and limited transparency law.

local-production.rationale: Swadeshi (preferring domestic and local goods) is a long-standing economic strand of the Sangh Parivar.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Sangh Parivar is a set of permanent organisations (RSS shakhas, VHP, BJP), not informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: sovereignty and nationalism lead adherents to place the constitution and national courts over international bodies.

religious-nation.rationale: Hindutva defines the nation by land, descent and Hindu culture rather than creed, and seeks a Hindu rashtra, so religion-linked culture defines the nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva's assertive sovereignty and Akhand Bharat nationalism, which rejects submission to any foreign power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on national unity and a strong centre; regional retention would weaken the unitary nation.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not doctrinal; Hindutva defends private property and does not frame the question in terms of common ownership of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: The RSS and BJP have long opposed communism as foreign and anti-cultural, though India has not made its defeat a stated mission.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from the BJP's mix of state-funded schemes such as Ayushman Bharat with private delivery.

religion-illusion.rationale: Hindutva treats Hindu culture and the holy land as central to nationhood and rejects the view that religion is an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from the BJP's market-liberalising economic record, though swadeshi strands are more sceptical.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from its social conservatism and non-Marxist economics; it does not tie women's equality to transforming the economy.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from social conservatism, which sees care as a family duty.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The movement promotes Hindi and Sanskritised vocabulary in place of Urdu and English borrowings, as part of its language policy.

treaties-binding.rationale: No clear doctrine; its unitary-nation stance and Article 370 abrogation cut against internal treaties, but it supports law-based process.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from its centralised nation-state aims and market economics; self-governing common-property communities are not a goal.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the Article 370 abrogation and support for Hindu settlement in Kashmir, though not a formal programme.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Integral humanism, the BJP's official philosophy, presents itself as a third way beyond capitalism and communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Hindutva defines the nation through the Hindu fatherland and holy land, so a historical and religious tie confers the stronger claim, as Savarkar's test and the Ayodhya campaign show.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Hindutva leaders do not generally deny it, though Golwalkar's 1939 text praised Nazi racial pride; the mainstream movement rejects denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The movement is socially conservative, and the leadership has been split since the 2018 Supreme Court decriminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The BJP governs democratically while critics note pressure on opponents; adherents do not state a policy of suppression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Hindutva favours protecting Hindu sentiment and some blasphemy-style laws exist in India, but it does not claim a state religion; adherents split.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva's nationalism and opposition to colonial rule.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva's hostility to jihad as a concept and its rejection of Islamic political claims.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Hindutva treats Hindu cultural nationalism as the basis of rule and rejects the idea of removing rulers for not following religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the BJP's electoral democracy with a strong centralised leadership; no doctrine on workplace participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Hindutva puts the Hindu nation first and rejects identity-based intersectional analysis; inferred from its cultural nationalism.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The movement is socially conservative and its leaders have resisted recognition of gender identity; inferred from BJP positions.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from the movement's social conservatism and religious views; not a doctrinal issue.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Hindutva sees the nation and culture as its core and rejects the left-right frame, though the BJP is placed on the right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from integral humanism's rejection of both capitalist and Marxist materialism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Hindutva holds that Islam cannot be fully integrated into the Hindu nation, and Golwalkar demanded non-Hindus adopt Hindu culture.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Hindutva grounds authority in the Hindu nation and the dharma, not a monotheist God, but not the people alone; the answer is mild.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Hindutva supports public expression of Hindu culture and has not supported religious dress bans, apart from Karnataka's 2022 school hijab order.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not a doctrinal issue; the movement does not address it directly.

social-market-economy.rationale: Integral humanism sits between capitalism and socialism and the BJP combines market reform with welfare schemes.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Hindutva stresses military strength and a strong defence, and the BJP's stance is strongly pro-army.

rich-first.rationale: The BJP's record is mixed and the movement favours growth, but swadeshi thought is wary of uneven gains; adherents split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The BJP government pursues strategic autonomy and avoids formal alliances, as inferred from its defence stance.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hindutva does not endorse hereditary rule; the Sangh Parivar styles itself as a mass movement and the BJP has criticised dynastic parties, notably the Congress.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not a defining issue; swadeshi strands favour local economic institutions but the BJP favours market banking, and the sources do not address mutual credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Swadeshi strands resist foreign economic pressure while the BJP government has liberalised and worked with the IMF, so adherents are split.

property-franchise.rationale: Hindutva defines the nation by culture and descent rather than property; the BJP governs a universal-franchise democracy and does not seek to restrict the vote by wealth.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva's traditional and nationalist framing, which does not stress ecofeminism; some Hindu thought links nature and the feminine, so only mildly disagree.

reification.rationale: A Marxist idea alien to Hindutva, which opposes Marxism and treats the nation and culture, not class, as the basic social reality.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Hindutva does not take up the question; adherents are split between nationalist critique of elite-owned media and support for the established order.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the BJP's constitutional framing and Savarkar's call for a state ruled by law; the sources do not address rule by decree.

racial-franchise.rationale: Hindutva defines the nation by shared land, descent and culture and treats non-Hindu minorities as outsiders, but the mainstream BJP accepts a universal franchise and does not propose limiting votes by group.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred from the BJP's strong emphasis on digital governance; the sources do not discuss political deliberation specifically.

open-government-data.rationale: The BJP promotes digital and open governance but is criticised on transparency, so adherents' position is mixed and the sources are silent.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Hindutva leaders oppose interfaith marriage in the 'love jihad' campaign, and several BJP-ruled states regulate marriage-linked conversion, though no state bans it outright.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Mainstream Hindutva organisations have called for avoiding Muslim traders in some local campaigns, but the BJP's official line disowns boycotts and adherents are split.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the movement's reliance on electoral majoritarian politics through the BJP; sortition is not part of its programme.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from Savarkar's rationalist, reformist stance toward scriptural orthodoxy, though current Sangh practice is mixed.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not a doctrinal issue; the BJP's record is business-friendly and Integral Humanism does not call for curbing fortunes.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Hindutva's social conservatism makes open service unlikely to be endorsed, though no doctrinal text addresses it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Hindutva makes Hindu culture the basis of the nation and a state promoting atheism contradicts that cultural nationalism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Hindutva's strong-state nationalism and security emphasis imply police and prisons stay; inferred from the BJP defence and law-and-order stance.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Hindutva treats Hindus as the nation's core and rejects guaranteed communal shares; Golwalkar says non-Hindus must adopt Hindu culture or stay subordinate.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Integral humanism and the RSS's service networks favour community and family-based help, while the BJP also expands welfare schemes.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the BJP has no doctrinal position and adherents are indifferent.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva's preference for strong organisational leadership over devolved participatory schemes.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents have no common view.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from social conservatism and opposition to some temple entry reforms; priestly offices are traditionally restricted.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Official statements favour women's dignity while traditional family roles are valued, so adherents split; inferred from the BJP's social conservatism.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Hindutva defines the nation by land, descent and culture; inferred that non-citizens would not get a vote.

rent-control.rationale: Not doctrinal; BJP economics mixes welfare and market policies, so adherents are split.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the BJP's pro-business, pro-innovation economics, which protects intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The RSS, Hindutva's core organisation, trains youth in uniformed, drilled shakhas for service to the nation.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: India's own weapons make a ban on territory unlikely, but foreign-based weapons would be opposed; adherents' view unclear.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva's sovereignty-focused nationalism; India hosts no foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Hindutva circles demand recognition of Kashmiri Pandit and Partition-era killings; the party line on general recognition is inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Not doctrinal; Hindutva economics has shifted between swadeshi and market liberalism.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Savarkar advocated militarising Hindus and Hindu tradition accepts just war; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Hindutva claims the Hindu nation is ancient, defined by a holy land and shared descent from Vedic times.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Hindu nationalists generally reject gender-constructivist theory; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Hindutva favours family-centred and traditional gender roles; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Nationalist movements honour balidan (sacrifice) for the motherland; inferred from the movement's nationalism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Hindutva frames politics as defending dharma and the Hindu holy land; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Savarkar's holy-land idea makes India the sacred centre for Hindus worldwide, and the VHP engages the diaspora; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: The RSS presents itself as a cultural organisation whose work of Hindu cultural revival precedes and underpins political power.

god-not-male.rationale: Hindu tradition worships goddesses as well as gods, so the Hindu divine is not exclusively male; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Hindutva does not subject scriptures to a feminist test; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Early texts like Golwalkar's are harsher, but the current movement is pro-business and does not press this; adherents split.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Hindutva stresses a unitary Akhand Bharat over regions built on ethnic or linguistic identity; inferred.

missingStatements.text: All citizens should be governed by the same civil laws regardless of their religion.
missingStatements.rationale: Hindutva leaders call for one common civil code and argue religion-based personal laws deepen division, and the BJP pledged it in 2024.

missingStatements.text: Religious conversion should be restricted by law.
missingStatements.rationale: BJP-ruled states have passed laws against conversion by force or through marriage, with prison terms of up to ten years.

missingStatements.text: The slaughter of cattle should be banned by law.
missingStatements.rationale: Hindutva supporters revere the cow and many BJP-ruled states have passed cattle-slaughter bans.

notes: Golwalkar's 1939 text is harsher toward minorities than the movement's present public line, which claims equal rights for all citizens and calls Hindutva cultural nationalism. Most economic, gender and technology answers are inferred (low) because Hindutva texts address identity, nation and culture rather than policy. Savarkar's own text was not opened; his claims are cited through Jaffrelot and Wikipedia.
